Container.Name: QBZ-Downloader
Container.Overview:
Qobuz downloader with a web dashboard for Hi-Res audio, metadata automation and local library management.
Search Qobuz and queue tracks, albums, artists or playlists; files are tagged from Qobuz metadata with cover art and lyrics, and organised on disk using your own folder and filename templates. The built-in library scanner reports duplicates, missing tags and tracks available at a higher quality than the copy you already have.
[b]Setting up[/b] [b]1.[/b] Set a dashboard password below. It is required: without one the dashboard refuses to serve a network address and binds to localhost inside the container, so the WebUI will not open. [b]2.[/b] Point [b]Music Library[/b] at the share you want files written to. [b]3.[/b] Start the container, open the WebUI and enter your Qobuz credentials under Settings.
Any application setting can also be supplied as an environment variable here (for example FOLDER_TEMPLATE or MAX_CONCURRENCY). A value saved in the dashboard takes precedence over the variable.

Config.Name: Dashboard Password
Config.Description: Required. Protects the dashboard, which can queue downloads and edit tags in your library. Without a password the app refuses to serve a network address and the WebUI will not be reachable.

Config.Name: Music Library
Config.Description: Where downloads are written. The library scanner reads this same path.

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: Database, settings and the key used to encrypt stored credentials. Keep this on appdata so it survives container updates.

Config.Name: Folder Structure
Config.Description: Folder template. {disc_folder} becomes CD1, CD2 ... on multi-disc releases and is empty on single-disc ones, so one template suits both.

Config.Name: Concurrent Downloads
Config.Description: How many downloads run at once.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User id the app runs as. Unraid's default is 99 (nobody); downloads are written with this owner, so it should match the rest of your shares.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group id the app runs as. Unraid's default is 100 (users).

Config.Name: UMASK
Config.Description: Permission mask for new files. 002 leaves them group-writable so other apps running as the users group can manage the library.
